parameters.content:
## Store · Slack router

A Slack app can send its button taps and modal submissions to one URL only. This is that URL, for every workflow in the store.

1. **Read the tap** reads the raw body Slack sent and the action or modal it came from.
2. **Sign the request** and **Pick the workflow** check Slack's signature (and that the request is under five minutes old), then look up the workflow: by the button's `action_id` prefix, then the modal's `callback_id`, then the channel the card is in.
3. **Pass the tap on** posts the exact same body and signature headers to that workflow's own webhook, so it checks the signature itself, as it would on its own.
4. **Answer Slack** returns whatever that workflow answered (a modal error, say) within Slack's three seconds.

The routes are in **Router settings**, written by build.py from system.json. Set `internal_url` to the address n8n can reach itself on (for example `http://localhost:5678`), so taps don't go out and back through your proxy.

nodes.name: Slack sends every tap
nodes.notes: Your Slack app's Interactivity Request URL (the manifest sets it). Raw body on, so the signature can be checked.

nodes.name: Read the tap
nodes.notes: Reads the raw body and pulls out what routing needs.

nodes.name: Router settings
nodes.notes: build.py writes routes from system.json. internal_url is how n8n reaches its own webhooks.

nodes.name: Sign the request
nodes.notes: HMAC of v0:timestamp:body with your Slack app's signing secret.

nodes.name: Pick the workflow
nodes.notes: Signature first. Then action_id prefix, modal callback_id, channel.

nodes.name: Pass the tap on
nodes.notes: Why HTTP: the workflow's own webhook checks the same signature, so it gets the exact body and headers. 2.5 s timeout keeps Slack's 3 s limit.

nodes.name: Answer Slack

parameters.responseBody: ={{ (() => { const b = $json.body ?? $json.data ?? ''; const t = typeof b === 'string' ? b : JSON.stringify(b); return /^\s*\{\s*"message"\s*:\s*"Workflow was started"/.test(t) ? '' : t; })() }}

nodes.notes: Hands back the workflow's own answer, such as a modal's validation errors. A timeout still answers 200, so Slack doesn't show an error.

nodes.name: Nothing to pass on
nodes.notes: 401 for a bad signature. 200 for link buttons and taps with no route, so Slack shows nothing.
